title: Hotels booked for shelter: what each was paid
question: Which hotels did the City book for shelter from 2020, what was each paid, per room where the room count is on file, and for how long?
finding: The payment file shows $297.6 million paid to 30 hotel payees on 31 room agreements that began under emergency purchasing rules, $228.7 million of it keyed under an emergency rule; the Board’s analyst counted 28 hotels, $224.7 million spent by June 28, 2022, and 2,288 rooms at the peak. Payments peaked at $115.6 million in fiscal 2021. The largest by far is Hotel Whitcomb: $88.1 million for 459 rooms, $191,846 a room over fiscal 2020 to 2023; the analyst put its average rate at $177.52 a room a night with meals and linen. Where the analyst’s table gives rooms (11 hotels), the total paid runs from $68,223 to $217,374 a room. 4 hotels were still being paid in fiscal 2024 or later (The Monarch Hotel, Adante Hotel, Cova Hotel and Days Inn San Francisco), and the Board approved 2 new one-year shelter leases of former programme hotels retroactively in 2025 (Lombard Hotel Group – Monarch Hotel; Roshan Investments LLC).
how: A booking agreement is a contract whose title says hotel and whose first payments were made by the Human Services Agency under a purchasing rule containing the word “emergency”; every payment on those contract numbers is then counted, whichever department or rule it was later keyed under. Payees are named as the payment file names them; “also registered as” lists names the project’s owner-groups tie to the same owner. Rooms are from the Budget and Legislative Analyst’s table of 11 agreements in its report of 13 July 2022, matched to payees by the hotel’s name or street address. Per room is all payments divided by rooms, over the whole stay, not a yearly figure. A payment is dated by its voucher number, so years can differ from the labelled years used in the exceptions file.
limits: The larger agreements went to the Board. The analyst’s report of July 2022 says that under the Mayor’s emergency proclamation any amendment to extend them beyond August 2022 “and to waive applicable restrictions in the Municipal Code requires approval of the Board of Supervisors by Ordinance”. The sums cover rooms, and at several hotels meals and linen as well, for up to three years of continuous use; a per-room total over three years is not a nightly rate. Room counts are on file for 11 hotels only. A payee name is the hotel’s trading name; the legal owner is named only where a Board file or the business registry gives it. Only payments on the room agreements are counted; whatever was paid to others for work inside the hotels is not. What would settle the price paid per night at each hotel: the booking agreements and their amendments, which state the nightly rate, the nights booked and what was included. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
